newsitem.title: USA: Intermediate muni bond yields fall over past week.
newsitem.headline: Intermediate muni bond yields fall over past week.

text.p: Intermediate municipal bond yields fell in the week ended Thursday, Delphis Hanover Corp said on Friday.
As the rest of the yield curve held steady, 5-year and 10-year municipal yields lost five basis points across the credit spectrum.
Yields fell to 4.50 percent for Aaa-rated 10-year munis and to 5.25 percent for Baa 10-years, Delphis said.
Meanwhile, one-year Aaa-rated bonds were unchanged for the week at 3.70 percent, and Baa-rated one-years held at 4.35 percent.
Long-term municipals lagged the Treasury market over the week.

The yield on the government long bond fell five basis points during the period to 6.44 percent, while thirty-year Aaa-rated municipal yields were unchanged at 5.25 percent. Yields were also unchanged for 30-year, Baa-rated bonds, which held at 5.90 percent.
Thirty-year, Aaa-rated munis yielded 81.5 percent of the Treasury long bond at the close Thursday.
The yield curves between one-year and 30-year bonds in both the triple-A category and Baa category were unchanged at 155 basis points.
Credit spreads were also unchanged on the week.
The credit spread between Aaa-rated and Baa-rated one-years was 65 basis points, while the 10-year spread held at 75.
Thirty-year bond credit spreads were unchanged at 65 basis points.
